extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains. Motivated by the critical roles across the full manipulation pipeline, RoboBench defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. To ensure realism, datasets are curated across diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation, drawing from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection. For planning, RoboBench introduces an evaluation framework that uses an MLLM as a world simulator, moving beyond symbolic matching to evaluate embodied feasibility by simulating whether predicted plans can achieve critical object-state changes under physical and visual constraints, enabling faithful assessment of long-horizon reasoning.

extraction.citeAs: Yulin Luo et al. RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv preprint arXiv:2510.17801v1, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Datasets are built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Instruction comprehension tasks adopt a paired explicit–implicit design, where explicit instructions are drawn from daily-life scenarios and implicit instructions are obtained by rewriting them into demand-based requests using LLMs. Perception reasoning datasets are constructed across robotic-centric, object-centric, scene-centric, and task-centric aspects, using real robot data with type and view metadata for template-based QA, combining curated static attributes with GPT-generated functional properties and distractors, leveraging Gemini-segmented video steps for temporal grounding with manual annotations for spatial and causal reasoning, and human-labeled bounding boxes for linking instructions to target objects. Generalized planning data is built from high-quality robotic videos, extracting frame sequences as standardized inputs. Gemini generates structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata), which are refined by human annotators. Failure analysis data includes execution-level failures collected from RoboMIND and labeled by experts, and planning-level failures synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection. High-quality robotic videos from sources such as Collaboration et al. (2023), Lin et al. (2024a), Liu et al. (2024b;c), Fang et al. (2023), Wu et al. (2024), Mu et al. (2023), Yang et al. (2024). Execution-level failures are collected from RoboMIND Wu et al. (2024).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Explicit instructions are rewritten into demand-based implicit requests using LLMs. Curated static attributes are combined with GPT-generated functional properties and distractors. Gemini-segmented video steps are used for temporal grounding. Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All data are standardized into multiple-choice QA where applicable. Frame sequences are extracted as standardized inputs for planning. A two-stage quality control process is adopted: data filtering during construction (general criteria for image quality and task validity, plus sub-benchmark tailored rules like excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks) and post-construction validation by professionally trained annotators. A majority-vote strategy is used where items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail undergo manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: MLLM- and human-provided annotations are used. Implicit instructions are generated by LLMs. Object-centric perception data includes GPT-generated functional properties and distractors. Scene-centric perception data uses manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes. Task-centric perception data uses human-labeled bounding boxes. For generalized planning, Gemini generates structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata), which are refined by human annotators. Execution-level failures are labeled by experts. Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy is adopted: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Models exhibit severe degradation on implicit instructions (average scores dropping by 30%), indicating weak grounding of indirect human goals. Models perform poorly on robot-view recognition and temporal grounding, revealing fragile spatial–temporal perception and limited embodiment awareness. Complex planning remains a primary bottleneck, with models struggling with dual-arm coordination and rare-object reasoning. Models show shallow affordance prediction, with even the best model (Gemini-2.5-Pro) being 17 points behind humans. Execution-level failure diagnosis remains the hardest dimension, with scores of 10–20 compared to 40–60 on planning error analysis, and even human evaluators achieving only 47.30. Current MLLMs exhibit only superficial embodied reasoning and world-modeling capabilities. Models struggle to maintain logical consistency, object grounding, and physical feasibility in long-horizon planning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It serves as a benchmark to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence. It is used for testing and validation of MLLMs across five dimensions: Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis.
